changed_in_1_4_4: Prompt entry_point REMOVED from prompt_topic_selected, prompt_editor_opened, prompt_saved, prompt_editor_dismissed and prompts_minimum_met; position removed from prompt_topic_selected. Product decision 25 Sep 2026: we measure WHICH topics are chosen (topic_id), not whether the tap came from a suggestion card or the browse sheet. enums §18 retired.
prompt_editor_dismissed gains is_edit: bool — the one job entry_point: "edit" did that nothing else carried (backing out of an edit vs. abandoning a new prompt).
The app-open entry_point on app_opened (cold|push|sms|whatsapp|email|deeplink) is unaffected.
changed_in_1_4_3: permission_status_changed — NEW, family G. The OS permission changed OUTSIDE our app and the reconciler noticed on a foreground read. permission_result only ever covered the answer to OUR dialog, so a user switching notifications off in Settings six weeks later was invisible and the server kept a stale grant. Carries type (§8), from/to (§24 permission_status), detected_on and in_flow. 21 Sep 2026, with the Profile 09 ticket.

Stated with it: the OS permission is READ, never remembered — one shared reconciler on every foreground, not a per-screen check — and it is not our consent record. consent_changed stays the consent event; this one is the device's answer changing under us.
changed_in_1_4_2: permission_prompted — trigger clarified only, no payload change: the pre-permission surface may be a full screen, not just a modal. Profile 09 (ProfileNotifications) is a full-screen pre-permission ask and fires it on view with type: "notifications". No new event was added for it — family G already covers prompted / os_sheet_shown / result / settings_opened, and the Profile 09 questions were answered from the registry. 21 Sep 2026.

No step event fires on the four out-of-bar profile screens (notifications, reachability, phonebook, location): profile_step_viewed requires an int step_index and enums §2 gives them none. See enums.json §2 note, 1.4.3.
changed_in_1_4_1: FAMILY F PROMPT COLLISION RESOLVED. Family F carried a second, v1.0 vocabulary for the written prompts — prompt_topic_picker_opened, prompt_topic_selected, prompt_answered, prompt_edited, prompt_removed — and prompt_topic_selected existed TWICE in this file with two different payloads. Family E wins: it is the vocabulary the Profile 07 ticket cites and the one with §17/§18/§19 behind it. The duplicate prompt_topic_selected row in F is DELETED (a name cannot mean two things); the other four are kept, emptied, and marked SUPERSEDED — DO NOT FIRE, each naming its family E replacement. Written prompts are instrumented in family E only.

prompt_topic_list_dismissed — NEW. The topic sheet closed without a topic being picked. The prompts screen had an abandonment event for the write sheet and none for the browse sheet; a cancel there was invisible. Added 16 Sep 2026, answering the Prompts implementation questions.

prompt_topic_selected — selection_index added, and the event is now scoped to suggestion and browse ONLY. Reopening a saved prompt no longer fires it: an edit is not a fresh choice of topic, and counting it double-counted topic demand. selection_index: 1 is the topic the user reached for first.

profile_step_completed — prompt_count added, optional and screen-scoped (profile_prompts). How many prompts the user held when Continue was pressed. The Profile 07 ticket specified it as count; the registry name is prompt_count and the ticket was corrected.
form_validation_failed — rule gains prompts_below_minimum, the prompts sibling of photos_below_minimum: Continue pressed with zero prompts saved.

dismiss_method — one canonical value set across every sheet (enums §23): close · backdrop · swipe · system_back. prompt_editor_dismissed had scrim / back and media_prompt_list_dismissed had cancel; both are migrated. Neither shipped, so nothing in the warehouse changes.

events.name: screen_viewed

payload.name: screen_id
payload.type: str — canonical snake_case key from enums.json §11. Stable forever; never re-used, never edited.

payload.name: screen_name
payload.type: str — the human label from enums.json §11, verbatim. What you search for in the analytics tool. May be edited when the screen is renamed.

payload.name: last_used
payload.type: str — OPTIONAL, SCREEN-SCOPED. Which auth method the user last signed in with. Only meaningful on a screen that offers a method list (signup_welcome_back, signup_create_account, connect_sso). OMIT everywhere else — it has no value on a profile step, and an empty string is worse than an absent property (decision 29).

payload.name: state
payload.type: str — OPTIONAL, SCREEN-SCOPED. For a screen whose registry row covers many states (§11 rule: one row per screen, not per state), this says which one. Only connect_sso uses it, and it is KNOWN BROKEN there — always "idle", because screen_viewed fires once on mount and the state changes afterwards. OMIT on every other screen. It cannot describe the DoB or verify-email states, which are carried by their own events (decision 29).

events.required_payload: screen_id, screen_name, referrer_screen_id — these three, on every screen, always. last_used and state are optional and screen-scoped; see each one. A flat payload list is not a statement that every property applies everywhere (decision 29).

events.name: prompt_topic_list_opened
events.trigger: The “Browse all 15 topics” control tapped, opening the topic sheet. Read against screen views of the step, this is how often the three suggestions were not enough.

events.name: prompt_topic_list_dismissed
events.trigger: The topic sheet closed WITHOUT a topic being picked — the X, the scrim, a swipe-down or the system back gesture. Picking a topic replaces the sheet with the write sheet and fires prompt_topic_selected instead, so this event and that one are mutually exclusive and together they close the browse sheet's funnel: opened (prompt_topic_list_opened) → picked or cancelled. Added 16 Sep 2026: the write sheet had an abandonment event and the browse sheet did not, so a user who opened all fifteen topics and closed the sheet was invisible. Read against prompt_topic_list_opened, a high rate means the fifteen are not the problem the suggestion cards were solving.

events.name: prompt_topic_selected

payload.name: selection_index
payload.type: int — 1-based count of topic selections in this visit to the step. 1 is the topic the user reached for FIRST, which is not the same question as which topic they saved.

events.trigger: A topic chosen — a suggestion card on the screen or a row in the browse sheet. The two are deliberately NOT distinguished: entry_point and position were removed on 25 Sep 2026 (taxonomy 1.4.4), because the question is which topics are chosen, not where. DOES NOT FIRE ON EDIT from v1.4.1: reopening a saved prompt is not a fresh choice of topic; prompt_editor_opened{is_edit:true} covers that. THE event that answers which topics people choose, and with selection_index, which one they tried first. topic_id from enums §17.

events.name: prompt_editor_opened
events.trigger: The write sheet mounted — on a suggestion card, on a row of the browse sheet, or on the pencil pip of a saved prompt. THIS IS THE EDIT EVENT: is_edit: true is the pencil being tapped, and from v1.4.1 it is the only event an edit fires at open (prompt_topic_selected no longer does). Paired with prompt_saved / prompt_editor_dismissed, this is the per-topic completion rate: how many people open a topic and how many finish it.

events.name: prompt_example_dismissed
events.trigger: The worked example hidden with its X. Low volume by design; if it is high, the example is in the way rather than helping.

events.name: prompt_char_limit_reached
events.trigger: The answer first reached 160 characters in this editor session. Fires once per session, not per keystroke. Says whether the cap is the right number — it is currently unvalidated.

events.name: prompt_saved
events.trigger: Save pressed with a non-empty answer. NEVER send the answer text — length_bucket only (enums §19). prompt_count is the number of prompts the user holds after this save.

events.name: prompt_editor_dismissed

payload.name: dismiss_method
payload.type: "close"|"backdrop"|"swipe"|"system_back" — enums.json §23. Was close|scrim|swipe|back until v1.4.1; migrated to the one canonical sheet vocabulary.

events.trigger: The write sheet closed without saving. THE abandonment event this screen is designed against: a user who opened a topic, typed something and left is the drop-off that was previously invisible. had_draft is what separates “changed their mind” from “could not finish”. is_edit (added 25 Sep 2026, replacing entry_point: "edit") separates backing out of an edit from abandoning a new prompt.

events.name: prompt_deleted
events.trigger: A saved prompt removed. Not reachable from the profile-creation screen (there is no delete there) — it exists for profile editing, and is registered here so that flow cannot invent a second name.

events.name: prompts_minimum_met
events.trigger: The first prompt was saved, so the step can be completed — fires once, on the first crossing. The prompts sibling of photos_minimum_met, and the single number that says whether this screen works.

events.name: media_screen_viewed

payload.name: preview_video_prompt_id
payload.type: str — enums.json §20; the prompt previewed on the empty video card at this view

events.trigger: The Media screen ("Show your face") finishes rendering. has_video / has_voice carry the entry state of BOTH slots, which is what makes every later retake or delete on this screen attributable to a user who already had an artefact — the question the two booleans exist to answer. Fires on every mount, including the return from an accepted recording, so the state change is visible as two consecutive views. Was type: "voice"|"video" until v1.4: one screen carries both cards, so the screen view is not per medium — the medium belongs on the acts below. The two preview ids record which prompt each empty card displayed, because from v1.4 that is server-ranked rather than fixed (decision 33) — without them the ranking cannot be evaluated against the behaviour it produced.
events.required_payload: screen_id, has_video, has_voice, and both preview_*_prompt_id + preview_source — every mount. WHAT WAS SHOWN IS NOT DERIVABLE AFTER THE FACT: the ranking changes, so a view that does not record the two prompts it displayed cannot be attributed later.

events.name: media_prompt_list_opened
events.trigger: "See the prompts" tapped, opening the prompt list for one medium. Replaces media_inspiration_opened (v1.4): the "Show me what works" inspiration sheet was removed from the kit on 16 Sep 2026 and the eleven-prompt list took its place, so topic_id no longer applies — the chosen prompt is carried by media_prompt_selected instead. has_existing separates opening the list with an empty card from reopening it over something already recorded.
events.required_payload: type is REQUIRED. One screen carries the video card and the voice card, and an event without type cannot be attributed to either.

events.name: media_prompt_selected

payload.name: was_previewed
payload.type: bool — true if this prompt was the one shown on the empty card at the time the list was opened

events.trigger: The commit CTA ("Film 10 seconds" / "Record 15 seconds") tapped with a row selected — the prompt the user actually took into the camera, not every row they tried on the way. STORE AND SEND THE ID, NEVER THE DISPLAY STRING (§20): the prompts are copy and will be edited. type scopes it, because the same eleven are offered for both media and "which prompt gets chosen" is a different answer for video than for voice. selections_before counts the rows tapped and abandoned first — a list that takes four taps to settle is a list that is too long. was_previewed is the feedback-loop guard: the previewed prompt is more visible than the other ten, so the ranking that feeds the preview is computed with those selections EXCLUDED (decision 33). An event without it makes the ranking self-reinforcing and unmeasurable.

events.name: media_prompt_list_dismissed

payload.name: dismiss_method
payload.type: "close"|"backdrop"|"swipe"|"system_back" — enums.json §23. cancel was renamed close in v1.4.1 so every sheet in the product shares one value set.

events.trigger: The prompt list closed without going to the camera — the X, the backdrop, a swipe-down, or the system back gesture. had_selection: true is a user who picked a prompt and then backed out, which is a different signal from one who read the list and left; both are the drop-off the list is accountable for. Uses dismiss_method, not method — see §8 on the two vocabularies that collided under method.

events.name: video_recording_started
events.trigger: Video capture actually begins on the recording screen — permission already granted, timer running. Was prompt_id: str until v1.4; renamed media_prompt_id because prompt_id is already the written-prompt key (§6, §17) and the two registries are unrelated. attempt counts takes of the same prompt, starting at 1, so a retake loop is readable without diffing timestamps.

events.name: video_prompt_recorded
events.trigger: "Use this clip" accepted on the review screen — NOT on Stop. Stopping produces a take; accepting produces the artefact, and only this event means the profile gained something. A take that is stopped and then retaken never fires it. The user returns to the Media screen, where the next media_screen_viewed carries has_video: true.

events.name: voice_recording_started
events.trigger: Voice capture actually begins on the recording screen — permission already granted, timer running. Was prompt_id: str until v1.4; renamed media_prompt_id because prompt_id is already the written-prompt key (§6, §17) and the two registries are unrelated. attempt counts takes of the same prompt, starting at 1, so a retake loop is readable without diffing timestamps.

events.name: voice_prompt_recorded
events.trigger: "Use this recording" accepted on the review screen — NOT on Stop. Stopping produces a take; accepting produces the artefact, and only this event means the profile gained something. A take that is stopped and then retaken never fires it. The user returns to the Media screen, where the next media_screen_viewed carries has_voice: true.

events.name: media_review_shown
events.trigger: Stop tapped, or the length cap reached, and the review screen mounts — play / retake / keep. The denominator for everything that follows a take: media_preview_played, media_retaken{from:"review"} and video_prompt_recorded / voice_prompt_recorded are all choices made on this screen, and none of them is interpretable without knowing how many takes reached it. stop_reason separates a user who finished early from one who ran out of seconds.

events.name: media_preview_played
events.trigger: Play tapped on the review screen. Fires per play with a running count, starting at 1 — whether people watch or listen back before keeping a take is the question the review screen exists to answer, and a single event with no count cannot tell a confident keep from a nervous one.

events.name: media_prompt_ranking_published

payload.name: media_prompt_id
payload.type: str — enums.json §20; the prompt now previewed for this medium

events.trigger: The ranking job publishes the preview prompt for one medium — once per medium per refresh, and ONLY when the published value changes. The audit trail for decision 33: a preview that moved has to be attributable to a sample and a window, or a drop in recording rate cannot be told apart from a bad prompt. Server-side; the client never ranks and never computes a preview locally.

events.name: media_retaken
events.trigger: Retake tapped — either on the review screen, discarding the take just made, or on a filled card on the Media screen, replacing something already saved to the profile. had_video / had_voice carry what the profile held at that moment, so a retake by a user who already has both media is distinguishable from a first-time loop.
events.required_payload: type and from are both REQUIRED. from is what separates a discarded draft from a replaced artefact; without it the two collapse into one number that means neither.

events.name: media_deleted
events.trigger: Delete tapped on a filled card on the Media screen — the artefact is removed from the profile and the card returns to empty. Deleting is not retaking: there is no replacement take, and collapsing the two would read a user giving up as a user trying again. had_video / had_voice are the state BEFORE the deletion.

events.name: field_display_opted_out

events.name: permission_prompted
events.trigger: Our own pre-permission surface shown, before any OS sheet — a modal OR a full screen. Profile 09 (ProfileNotifications) is the full-screen case and fires this on view with type: "notifications"; it does not fire when the screen is skipped because the OS status is already determined.

events.name: permission_result
events.trigger: User responds to OS permission dialog

events.name: permission_settings_opened
events.trigger: Deep-link to OS App Settings tapped

events.name: permission_status_changed

payload.name: from
payload.type: str — enums.json §24 permission_status; the last value the client synced

payload.name: to
payload.type: str — enums.json §24 permission_status; the value just read

payload.name: in_flow
payload.type: bool — true when the change is detected while the user is still inside profile creation

events.required_payload: type, from, to and detected_on always. from is what the SERVER was last told, not what the screen last saw — a change the client never synced is exactly the case this event exists for.
events.trigger: The OS permission status read on launch or foreground differs from the last value the client synced: the user changed it outside our app (Settings, an OS update, a Focus mode, Android's per-channel switches) or a restore carried a different one in. NOT the answer to our own dialog — that is permission_result, and the two must never both fire for one act. Emitted by the shared permission reconciler, not by a screen.

events.name: consent_changed
events.trigger: A consent toggle changed, in either direction — on:false is the opt-out, on:true the opt-in. TWO PLACES FIRE THIS. (1) The marketing checkbox on the profile Email screen: channel:"marketing_email", surface:"profile_creation". The address itself is not a consent — it is used for password resets and support replies regardless; the checkbox governs marketing mail alone, so an unchecked box means no marketing, not no email (decision 28). (2) The six Stay reachable toggles: channel is one of the other six values. surface is required on both — a consent record that cannot be traced to where it was given cannot be honoured.

events.name: reachability_saved
events.trigger: “Save preferences” tapped — the state the user actually leaves the screen in, which per-toggle events cannot reconstruct. A skip fires profile_step_skipped step_id:"reachability"

reconciled_with_code: ShowUp app + server tracking catalogue, 7 September 2026 (35 events). Names for the built flows follow the code; unbuilt events keep their spec names.
screen_identity_note: Two properties, on purpose. screen_id is the stable machine key and never changes. screen_name is the human label and is what a person searches for in the analytics tool. Only screen_viewed carries both; every other event carries screen_id alone and joins to it. Both values come from the enums.json §11 registry — never typed at a call site.
